I ask Tim Constantine with you on the Capitol Hills Show, join me today, former Secretary of State, Mike Pompeo. Hi
how are you? Tim, it's great to be with you again.

Traditionally, from administration to administration, even when parties change, America's foreign policy has remained somewhat constant. The last couple of administrations, that's not necessarily true. How much of Trump's foreign policy has been preserved by the Biden administration?

Good. That's not nearly enough. And when I say not enough, I just think it's actually true that we are more at risk today from external threats than we were when we walked out in January of 2021. There's a war in Europe. We had a Chinese balloon fly over our country, our southern border is porous. These are the tip of the iceberg in terms of risk, and the Biden administration has made decisions that allowed each of these to happen.
Is there one maybe successful thing that you'd point out or one piece of continuity that you would point out that the Biden administration has done?

Yes, of course. There's a couple, actually. They've done pretty good work with respect to the Chinese Communist Party. I hope they'll lean in more. The fact they allowed this balloon to fly over the country was a mistake. But in terms of recognizing the threat, they have stayed consistent. And we flipped. 50 years of U.S. policy where it had been engaged, engaged, engaged. Trump administration, I led the charge, said, nope, that just doesn't work for the American people, for families here at home. And the Biden administration has kept that stance. They haven't come back to say these are just friendly competitors. They've now recognized the threat from the CCP.

Well, there's Ukrainian kids being killed, and that's the responsibility of Vladimir Putin. An unprovoked war is his cause. But we had deterrence, Tim. For four years, Vladimir Putin didn't invade Europe. He invaded it in 2014. For four years he didn't and then as soon as we left he went after it again that is because he perceived the risk as being lower. I'm convinced of that whether it was the failure in Afghanistan where we got thirteen Americans killed whether it was President Biden's statement that says you know a minor incursion that might be okay. Those are the things that Vladimir Putin in his mind says, boy, my risk is low. And so we could have done more to deter. The fact that the Biden administration is providing systems to the Ukrainians to help them defend themselves, I applaud. But man, they've been slow. And man, they've been late. And man, they have feared Vladimir Putin being provoked. I have to tell you, I think he's done been provoked. And the cautiousness has allowed this war to continue to go on. We could have ended this thing more quickly. We could have provided these systems to them at the front end, and the Ukrainians would have done the heavy lifting. And I'm convinced we wouldn't be where we are today.
